meta.project: GOLD1 — Gold engagement ring buying research
meta.scope_statement: This pass covers 13 ring listings from 3 U.S. retailers (Blue Nile, Mejuri, Brilliant Earth) plus a 3-retailer policy/contact review. It is a verified starting set, not a market census. Every price below was read from the retailer's own page in this session on 2026-10-22; no price came from a search-result snippet, a blog, or memory.
no_hallucination_policy: Every price, specification and policy claim in this dataset has a source_url that was opened in this session.
If a value could not be confirmed from an official page it is stored as null and carries a flag. Values are never inferred, averaged, or filled in from memory.
Search-engine snippets are treated as untrusted. Two snippet-vs-page price discrepancies were caught and published as flags F-02 and F-03.
Prices are point-in-time. Retailer prices change; the checked_on date is part of every row and must be re-verified before any purchase decision.
Gold-value arithmetic never substitutes for a measured gram weight. No listing in this pass published a gram weight, so no row carries a computed melt value.
meta.price_caveat: “Setting price” / “Setting Only” excludes the centre diamond. 9 of 13 rows are setting-only prices and must not be read as the price of a finished ring.
meta.purity_caveat: A karat stamp or a “14K” product title is a seller claim, not proof of composition. 16 CFR Part 23 permits a quality mark only with the maker's mark beside it, and even a correctly applied mark says nothing about whether this specific item is what it claims to be. Physical verification (XRF or equivalent) after delivery remains the only confirmation.

flags.title: Blue Nile 18K ring description contradicts its own metal specification
flags.detail: The Petite Nouveau Six-Prong Solitaire page is titled and specified as 18K Yellow Gold, but the product description on the same page says the ring is “crafted in polished 14k white gold”. One of the two statements is wrong. Do not buy without written confirmation of the metal from the seller.

flags.title: Search-engine snippet price ($925) does not match the live page ($1,420)
flags.detail: A search result for Blue Nile item 203268 displayed “$925 (Setting Price)”. The live page read $1,420 on 2026-10-22. The live page is authoritative and is what this dataset records. This is why snippets are never used as price evidence in this project.

flags.title: Mejuri Bold Diamond Eternity Ring: snippet $2,800 vs live $2,900
flags.detail: A search snippet showed $2,800; the live page on the 14k white gold / natural diamond selection showed “From $2,900”. Mejuri prices vary by material, stone and size, and “From” prices move with size. The dataset records the material- and date-stamped value.

flags.title: No listing in this pass publishes the ring's weight in grams (0 of 13)
flags.detail: Gram weight is the single number needed to compare price against gold value. Blue Nile, Mejuri and Brilliant Earth pages publish width and thickness but not weight. Until a seller supplies weight in writing, the gold-value calculator cannot be applied to any row here. Ask the seller for the weight in grams before paying.

flags.title: No listing publishes hallmark or maker's mark details (0 of 13)
flags.detail: None of the pages reviewed state what is stamped inside the band. Under the National Stamping Act a quality mark must be accompanied by the maker's trademark, so the absence of published hallmark information is a legitimate pre-purchase question, not proof of a problem. Verify the stamp in person and with XRF after delivery.

flags.title: Setting-only prices are not ring prices (9 of 13 rows)
flags.detail: Blue Nile and Brilliant Earth quote “Setting Price” / “Setting Only”, which excludes the centre diamond. A $1,000 setting plus a diamond is a materially different purchase. Mejuri's 4 rows are complete-ring prices, so the two groups must never be compared directly.

flags.title: “From” prices on Mejuri change with ring size
flags.detail: Two Mejuri rows show “From $…”, meaning the selected size determines the final price. The recorded number is the lowest displayed price on the date checked.

flags.title: Blue Nile return window not confirmed on the pages read
flags.detail: The product pages show a “Free Returns” badge and link to a Returns Policy, but do not state the number of days. The specific policy page was not opened in this pass, so the window and any resizing/custom exclusions are unverified.

flags.title: Brilliant Earth return window not confirmed on the page read
flags.detail: The page shows “Free Shipping & Returns” and “Free 1-Year Resizing”, but not the return window or exclusions. The dedicated returns page was not opened in this pass.

flags.title: Independent reputation research not performed in this pass
flags.detail: No BBB profile, state consumer-protection complaint record or independent review corpus was read for any of the three retailers. Contact information was verified (phone or store locator), but seller reputation is not yet independently verified for any retailer in this dataset.

flags.title: Regulatory text confirmed via official excerpts, not full section reads
flags.detail: 16 CFR Part 23 was confirmed through the official eCFR index entry and the Federal Register final-rule text (including Note 2 to §23.10 and §23.4). Sections were not read in full, and a guessed FTC business-guidance URL returned 404.

flags.title: Credit-card purchase-protection advice is not backed by a citation yet
flags.detail: The recommendation to pay by credit card is standard consumer practice but no official CFPB/FTC page was retrieved in this pass to support specific dispute rights. Treat the payment row on the checklist as advice, not as a verified legal claim.

flags.title: Spot gold is a single commercial reading, and the page disagreed with itself by $1.08
flags.detail: The recorded spot ($4,026.79/oz at 2026-10-22 07:07 NY) is from a commercial aggregator, not an exchange feed. A second ticker on the same page showed $4,025.71. The calculator therefore treats spot as an editable input and stamps every result with the number used.

flags.title: Brilliant Earth 18K ring uses 14K white gold prongs
flags.detail: The product detail lists “Prong metal: 14K White Gold” on an 18K yellow gold ring. This is a mixed-metal construction, not an error, but it means not all metal in the ring is 18K.

flags.title: Retailers named but not vetted in this pass
flags.detail: Costco, James Allen, Tiffany & Co., Aurate and Derco Diamonds appeared during source discovery but were not vetted. No price for them is recorded anywhere in this dataset. Listing them here prevents anyone from mistaking absence for a negative finding.

complete_ring_price_range_usd.note: Mejuri rows; includes a plain band and diamond bands — not like-for-like

findings: The two facts that decide whether a ring is fairly priced — gram weight and hallmark — are published on none of the 13 listings. Both must be obtained in writing from the seller before payment.

The cheapest verified 14K solitaire setting here is $935 (Blue Nile Classic Comfort Fit); the cheapest 18K setting is $1,240 (Blue Nile Classic Six-Prong). They are different models, so the $305 difference mixes metal cost with design — it is not a gold-value calculation.
Setting-only and complete-ring prices are mixed together in most online 'engagement ring price' comparisons. Keeping them separate is the single most useful structural decision in this dataset.

Mejuri is the only retailer here whose pages use the words 'solid gold' explicitly; Blue Nile and Brilliant Earth state karat only. That is a wording gap, not evidence of plated goods, but it is the exact phrase the checklist asks for.
All three retailers publish a warranty (Blue Nile's is limited to items of $1,000 or more); none publishes a hallmark or gram-weight policy. Warranty coverage is not a purity guarantee.
